summary.whatChanges: The AWS Lambda streaming adapter now pipes the response body through Node's `stream/promises` pipeline via an async generator instead of writing chunks in a loop, so writes respect the destination's backpressure and the handler waits for the stream to finish. Adds runtime tests covering pacing and mid-stream body errors.
behaviorChanges: Lambda response streaming honors the response stream's highWaterMark, so the web ReadableStream is no longer drained far ahead of what the destination has written
The streaming handler promise resolves only after the response stream has actually finished writing, not just after the last write() call
Errors thrown mid-body now propagate through the pipeline and are handled by the handler's existing error path (logged as 'Error processing request:') instead of being silently unhandled
On error, the writable is destroyed by the pipeline rather than being ended normally
risks: `pipeline` destroys the writable on error; Lambda's response stream may then terminate the response differently than the previous end()-only behavior
Depends on `node:stream/promises`, tightening the adapter's coupling to a Node runtime
Slower per-chunk delivery when the destination is slow could change timing-sensitive streaming responses (e.g. SSE latency)
